The diagnostic timing baseline required an explicit main-actor annotation under Swift 6.  The final helper retains the exact-output comparison and diagnostic timings without a speed threshold.

Intel passed 190 Swift tests, 55 fixtures, native components, and exact formatting, then the real-window Find check caught unavailable commands.  The older compiler also required an explicitly typed Sendable timing closure.

Both hosts passed 190 Swift tests, 55 fixtures, native components, and exact formatting.  Find remained unavailable in a key Reader despite shared scene commands.  The final correction uses public key-window notifications and weak references to owned text views; all original menu and native Find-bar assertions remain.
The registry candidate required fully qualified NSWindow notification names.  The correction keeps the same public notifications, weak text-view associations, and native assertions.

Both hosts reached the native interface check, which still observed unavailable Reader Find items before preparing the lazy native menu.  The final checker calls the public menu delegate as AppKit does before display, asserts the active Reader target independently, and retains every command-availability and native Find-bar assertion.  Only the checker changed in the final source.
